notes.coptic_form: ⲡⲙⲟⲩ ⲛⲧⲙ̄ⲏⲧⲉ ⲉⲧⲉ ⲛⲧⲁⲥ ⲡⲉ ⲧϩⲩⲗⲏ
notes.decision: Translated 'the Death of the Midst, which is the Hyle' — direct correspondential identification: the Manichaean Death-of-the-Midst (the cosmic death-zone) IS Matter. Capitalized 'Death of the Midst' as cosmic principle.
Greek ὕπαρξις 'existence, substance.' Rendered 'an existence' rather than 'a substance' to preserve the more abstract ontological sense; ⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁ is the standard term for 'substance.'

Read as qualitative 'dead' (= ⲙⲟⲟⲩⲧ qualitative), modifying ⲥⲱⲙⲁ. The phrase ⲟⲩⲥⲱⲙⲁ ⲉϩⲙⲁⲩⲧ = 'a body, dead' fits the context of the chapter's discussion of the body of death and the elements without life (line 8).
Treated triple ⲛⲁ as decorative chapter-heading sigla framing the title, parallel to the > < marks bracketing the running title in the header. Rendered as ‹ ... › quotation guillemets.

Greek ἀρετή 'virtue, excellence.' Chapter title 'Concerning the Virtue of the Firmaments' — ⲁⲣⲉⲧⲏ here designates the cosmic-functional excellence/power of the firmaments as established by the Living Spirit's rich son.

Lycopolitan verbal form of 'receive/take' (paralleled by line 19 ⲁϩⲧ ⲁⲧⲟⲟⲧϥ 'received into his hand'). Probable reduced form of ⲁⲙⲁϩⲧⲉ 'grasp, take hold' or related receiving-verb. Translated 'received' for both occurrences.

Greek ἀπαρχή 'firstfruits.' Cosmogonic technical term: 'the firstfruits of his Five Sons' = the captured light-elements taken by the dark powers in the primordial battle, paralleling 'the firstfruits of the firmaments' in line 19-20.

ⲭⲁⲗⲭ = Lyc. reflex of ϫⲱⲗϫ 'mingle, twist together' (in accumulated vocab); ⲣ̄-ⲥⲧⲁⲩⲣⲉ = σταυρόω 'crucify.' The cosmic crucifixion of the archontic host — they are bound and stretched out across the cosmic frame, mingled with the captured light. Manichaean technical motif of the cosmic cross.

ⲣⲁⲡⲡⲉ tentatively rendered 'their members' on contextual grounds (the archontic host being mingled and dispersed); etymology unclear, possibly Lyc. variant of ⲣⲱⲡⲉ 'limb' or related body-part term. ⲟⲩⲁⲧϩ̄ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ likely = ⲟⲩⲱⲧⲡ̄ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'pour/transfer forth.' The whole reading is provisional.

'A rich one in power' — the rich son of the Living Spirit. ⲧⲟⲁⲙ = ϫⲟⲙ 'power' (Lyc.). The 'rich one in power' is the cosmic figure commissioned to set up the firmaments — likely identifiable with one of the Five Sons of the Living Spirit (possibly the King of Honor or the Great Builder).

notes.coptic_form: ⲧⲛ[ⲧⲁⲛⲧ] ⲙⲡⲓⲣⲏⲧⲉ ⲛ̄ⲧϩⲉ ... ⲙⲛ̄ ⲟⲩⲣⲱⲙⲉ ⲛⲁⲣⲭⲓⲧⲉⲕⲧⲱⲛ
notes.decision: The Living Spirit being likened to a human architect who builds the king's house — standard Manichaean cosmogonic typology where the cosmic Builder corresponds to the earthly architect. The simile continues into the architectural details (houses, exedrae) of lines 29-31.
Likely Greek ἐξέδρα 'exedra, outer/recessed room' adapted to Coptic with ⲁϩⲛ- prefix (= ⲁϩⲟⲩⲛ 'into'). Architectural term fitting the king's-house simile. Translated 'outer rooms.'
